description: The multi-provider seam already reduces a new agent CLI to ONE dispatch case in `engine/agent.sh` `_run_provider()` — but nothing documents that recipe, and the surrounding roster surfaces (the two validator lists in `engine/agent.sh` + `bin/chief cmd_run`, the `--<provider>` CLI shorthands, `chief models`, `templates/config`, README) drift independently, as Amp proves. AMP CODE TRUTH, per the 2026-08-11 audit: `amp` is ACCEPTED by both validators (`bin/chief` `claude|devin|opencode|amp)`, `engine/agent.sh` provider check) and has a FIRST-CLASS dispatch case (`amp --dangerously-allow-all`, prompt on stdin) — it is NOT an alias of anything — yet `engine/driver.sh`'s header calls it 'a legacy alias', both invalid-provider error messages name only three providers, `--model` is silently ignored for it, there is no `--amp` shorthand, no `chief models` case, no mention in README/`templates/config`, and no `test/provider.sh` coverage. This tasklist (a) documents the onboarding recipe, (b) generalizes the hermetic scripted-fake conformance test so a new provider = one dispatch case + one registered fixture, and (c) settles Amp's status by applying that recipe to it — first-class everywhere or explicitly retired, no third state. Scope: `docs/`, `test/`, `engine/agent.sh`, `engine/driver.sh` (comment), `bin/chief`, `templates/config`, README; editing `engine/`/`bin/` bumps `VERSION`.

userStories.title: Document the provider onboarding recipe
userStories.description: Write the checklist that makes adding an agent CLI a one-case + one-fixture change, enumerating every roster surface so none is forgotten.
acceptanceCriteria: A `docs/providers.md` (or an equivalently discoverable doc linked from README + ROADMAP) documents the onboarding recipe as an explicit checklist: the `_run_provider()` dispatch case in `engine/agent.sh` (non-interactive/print mode, permission bypass flag, prompt delivery — stdin vs. prompt-file, like devin — and the `--model`/`$MODEL` wiring or a recorded decision that the CLI has no model flag), the TWO validator lists (`engine/agent.sh` + `bin/chief cmd_run`) and their error strings, the optional `--<provider>` shorthand in `cmd_run`, the `chief models` case, the `templates/config` roster comment, the README provider mentions/command-table row, and the conformance fixture from US-2

The doc states the invariants a provider case must satisfy: runs non-interactively from a piped prompt, preserves its own exit status for limit classification (`_is_rate_limit`), and needs no chief-side state beyond the dispatch case

The doc explains how usage-limit detection interacts with a new provider: `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERN`/`RATE_LIMIT_STATUS_PATTERN` are provider-output-based, so a provider whose limit phrasing isn't covered must extend the pattern (with a test), or its limit stops will be misread as stalls
Docs-only for this story (no engine edits yet); markdown links resolve

userStories.title: A hermetic, roster-driven provider conformance harness
userStories.description: Generalize test/provider.sh's per-provider scripted fakes into a parameterized conformance harness, so registering one fake + one expected-invocation line IS the test for a new provider.
acceptanceCriteria: The hermetic provider test (extend `test/provider.sh` or add `test/provider-conformance.sh` wired into `test/all.sh`) drives `engine/agent.sh` against a scripted fake CLI on `PATH` for EVERY provider the validators accept, asserting per provider: the exact argv the engine composes (recorded by the fake), prompt delivery on the documented channel (stdin vs. `--prompt-file`), `--model` propagation where supported, and that a fake emitting `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>` after a commit ends the loop with exit 0

The harness is data-driven: adding a provider means registering one fake script + one expected-invocation entry — no new test scaffolding — and the doc from US-1 points at the exact registration point
A roster-drift guard asserts the provider lists in `engine/agent.sh` and `bin/chief` accept the same set, so the two validators can never silently diverge again
Fully hermetic (temp `CHIEF_*` prefixes, fake CLIs on `PATH`, no network, never touches `~/.chief`); `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; bash 3.2 compatible; existing `test/*.sh` still pass

userStories.title: Settle Amp: first-class everywhere, or explicitly retired
userStories.description: Apply the US-1 recipe to Amp and eliminate the contradictory half-state the audit found. Default expectation: promote it (the dispatch case exists and works); retiring instead is acceptable only with a recorded rationale and removal from BOTH validators.
acceptanceCriteria: The false 'amp remains a legacy alias' comment in `engine/driver.sh` is corrected to the code truth (amp is its own dispatch case, not an alias), whichever way the status is settled

If PROMOTED: both invalid-provider error strings name amp; a `--amp` shorthand joins `--claude`/`--devin`/`--opencode` in `cmd_run`; the `--model` stance is settled (wired to amp's model flag if its CLI has one, otherwise documented as unsupported and rejected or warned on, never silently ignored); `templates/config`'s roster comment, README's provider prose + `chief run --provider` row, `chief models`' help text, and `docs/providers.md` all list amp; an amp fixture joins the US-2 conformance roster asserting its argv (`--dangerously-allow-all`) and stdin prompt delivery

If RETIRED instead: amp is removed from BOTH validators and the dispatch case, the removal and its rationale are recorded in `docs/providers.md` + ROADMAP, and a config that still sets amp fails with an actionable error naming the supported roster

ROADMAP.md's Current State provider line and the provider-breadth row agree with each other and with the settled code state; editing `engine/`/`bin/` bumps `VERSION` (`test/version-bump.sh` green); full suite green
